learning_outcomes.text: Apply the acquired knowledge to identify, formulate and solve problems in broad contexts, being capable of integrating them by working in multidisciplinary teams
Understand the impact of engineering on the environment, the sustainable development of society and the importance of working in a professional and responsible environment.
Communicate knowledge and conclusions, both orally and in writing, to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.

syllabus_topics: Air pollution and control of atmospheric emissions.
Global and local effects produced by atmospheric pollution.
Water pollution and technologies for its treatment.
Water pollutants and parameters indicating its pollution.
Technologies for the treatment of urban and industrial wastewater.
Management and treatment of solid waste.
teaching_methods: Presentation and reflection session on environmental volunteer work

assessment_methods.method: Presentation and reflection session on environmental volunteer work

assessment_rules: To pass the course, a final grade of 5.0 or higher is required. In the progressive and ordinary evaluation paths, the final grade is calculated from the first partial exam (45%, minimum 4.0), the second partial exam (45%, minimum 4.0), and the presentation and reflection session on environmental volunteer work (10%, no minimum grade required for this component). Environmental volunteer work itself has a 0% weight and is not recoverable. Students can resit partial exams in the ordinary global evaluation if they did not take them, scored below 5.0, or wish to improve their grade. For extraordinary evaluation, the final grade consists of a final exam covering all topics (90%) and the grade from the environmental volunteer work presentation session (10%).
